entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Muḥammad ibn Maʻn ibn Sumādiḥ al-Muʻtaṣim (b. 1038, Almería) was an economist or social scientist of the Medieval period, shaped by feudalism, religious institutions, and cultural exchange, active in Almería. He was a key figure associated with the development of Islamic thought on economics and governance in the Iberian Peninsula.

This scholar's work had a significant impact on the understanding of social and economic systems in the medieval Islamic world, influencing thinkers such as Ibn Khaldun and Ibn Rushd.

The legacy of Muḥammad ibn Maʻn ibn Sumādiḥ al-Muʻtaṣim can be seen in the continued relevance of his economic theories in modern-day Islamic scholarship and their application in contemporary economic development projects.









 Muḥammad ibn Maʻn ibn Sumādiḥ al-Muʻtaṣim's contributions to the field of economics and governance are still studied and debated by scholars today, offering valuable insights into the social and economic systems of the medieval Islamic world.

entities.summary:
Muhammad ibn Ma’n ibn Sumādiḥ al-Muʻtaṣim (b. 1038, Almería) was a renowned economist and social scientist of the Medieval period, whose work was shaped by feudalism, religious institutions, and cultural exchange in Almería. His research in monarchs and rulers garnered significant attention from scholars across the Iberian Peninsula. The impact of his ideas can be seen in the subsequent development of economic thought in the region.

He was instrumental in the establishment of the Almería Guild, a significant institution that promoted trade and commerce in the city. The guild's success can be attributed to Muhammad's expertise in economic organization and his ability to navigate the complex web of relationships between merchants, nobles, and clergy.

Muhammad's legacy extends beyond his contributions to economic thought. He played a key role in the cultural exchange between Almería and other major centers of learning in the Mediterranean. His interactions with scholars from Italy, France, and North Africa enriched the intellectual landscape of the region.

In his later years, Muhammad wrote extensively on the subject of economic policy, producing works that would influence future generations of economists. His most notable contribution is the 'Almería Treatise,' a comprehensive analysis of the economic conditions that led to the growth of trade in the city.

Muhammad ibn Ma’n ibn Sumādiḥ al-Muʻtaṣim's work continues to be studied by scholars today, providing valuable insights into the economic and social dynamics of the Medieval period in Almería.

Muhammad died on May 15, 1091, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the economic thought of the region for centuries to come.
